title: Must, Was to: Haber de + Infinitive

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *haber de* + infinitive from B2 Unit 26: a formal way to say a duty (*han de*, *he de*) and, in stories, *había de* or *habría de* for what was going to happen later. Agreements and rulings use it for what States must do, and it also fits the history of a struggle.

items.spanish: Los Estados han de proteger a las personas que defienden el territorio.
items.english: States must protect the people who defend the land.

items.spanish: Las comunidades han de ser consultadas antes de un proyecto.
items.english: Communities must be consulted before a project.

items.spanish: He de reconocer que la información es todavía limitada.
items.english: I must admit that the information is still limited.

items.spanish: Aquel caso habría de llegar al tribunal de Pastaza en 2019.
items.english: That case was to reach the court of Pastaza in 2019.

sections.content: *Haber de* changes with the person (*he de*, *has de*, *ha de*, *hemos de*, *han de*); *hay que* never does. Do not drop the *de*: not *los Estados han proteger*.
